output.paper_title: Adaptive Tensor Sparsification for Resource-Constrained Graph Neural Networks

core_summary.problem_statement: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) suffer from severe memory bottlenecks when scaling to massive web-scale graphs, primarily due to dense neighborhood aggregation tensors that quickly overwhelm edge GPU and accelerator memory during forward propagation.
core_summary.methodology: The authors introduce Adaptive Tensor Sparsification (ATS), which computes dynamic feature saliency thresholds per graph node, pruning low-magnitude aggregation messages prior to inter-layer matrix multiplication.
core_summary.algorithmic_contributions: A threshold-based pruning kernel with linear time complexity O(|E|), coupled with an error-compensating backward gradient estimator that restores dropped activations during the backward pass.
core_summary.key_findings: The method reduces intermediate memory footprints by up to 60% across benchmark social graphs while preserving within 1% of baseline link-prediction accuracy without requiring architecture retraining.
core_summary.plain_language_explanation: Rather than calculating updates from every single neighboring node, ATS selectively listens only to the most informative neighbors, dramatically saving computer memory while getting almost identical prediction results.

project_extensions.title: Quantized Integer Aggregation on Edge Microcontrollers
project_extensions.proposed_modification: Combine ATS dynamic pruning with 8-bit integer (INT8) quantization in the neighborhood aggregation operator.
project_extensions.problem_addressed: Edge embedded hardware lacks floating-point tensor units, creating latency bottlenecks even with pruned message sizes.
project_extensions.expected_benefit: Expected reduction in peak SRAM consumption and expected throughput gains on microcontroller architectures without structural model retraining.
project_extensions.success_metric: Maintain under 35ms inference latency per 500-node subgraph on ARM Cortex-M55 emulator with <2% drop in F1 score.
implementation_plan: Export ATS sparse matrices into standard Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) INT8 format.
Write custom INT8 fixed-point aggregation kernel for ARM CMSIS-NN.
Profile execution cycles and cache misses across synthetic citation network datasets.
project_extensions.evaluation_plan: Measure inference latency, memory high-water mark, and macro-F1 score on standard benchmark graph datasets.

project_extensions.title: Temporal Graph Saliency Cache for Dynamic Streaming Networks
project_extensions.proposed_modification: Implement an LRU saliency score cache that reuses computed neighborhood importance weights across consecutive temporal timesteps.
project_extensions.problem_addressed: Recomputing saliency thresholds from scratch at every incoming graph update wastes computational cycles on stable connections.
project_extensions.expected_benefit: Expected reduction in redundant threshold computations on dynamic streaming networks with moderate node churn.
project_extensions.success_metric: Targeting a 30-40% reduction in total FLOPs per graph snapshot with exact parity in classification outputs.
implementation_plan: Design timestamp-aware eviction policy for node saliency vectors.
Implement sliding-window invalidation mechanism for high-activity nodes.
Benchmark against vanilla continuous re-evaluation across evolving graph streams.
project_extensions.evaluation_plan: Compare end-to-end wall-clock throughput and cache hit rate against un-cached baseline on dynamic datasets.

project_extensions.title: Hardware-Aware Sparsification for Mobile WebGL Visualizers
project_extensions.proposed_modification: Port the ATS pruning logic to client-side WebAssembly and WebGPU shaders for real-time interactive browser graph exploration.
project_extensions.problem_addressed: Client-side browser graph visualization drops below 30 FPS when rendering dense subgraphs exceeding 10,000 vertices.
project_extensions.expected_benefit: Expected improvement in browser render frame rates and responsiveness during real-time user panning and exploration.
project_extensions.success_metric: Achieve consistent 60 FPS rendering on mid-tier mobile browsers for graphs with up to 25,000 nodes.
implementation_plan: Translate PyTorch sparse aggregation routines into WebGPU compute shaders.
Integrate dynamic node filtering with client-side particle rendering.
Conduct automated frame-rate profiling across desktop and mobile devices.
project_extensions.evaluation_plan: Record average frames per second (FPS) and memory heap consumption during continuous canvas pan/zoom interactions.
